## macOS

<a id="macos-0.3.10"></a>

### macOS 0.3.10 (2026-10-22)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.10)

The [full release notes](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.10) begin with a notice to read before opening this build.

This update adds an optional, more accurate speech model, starts recording
sooner after an idle hotkey press, and fixes a freeze after model downloads.

#### Speech model choice

- **Settings → Dictation → Speech Model** now offers Parakeet Ultra alongside
  the default Parakeet TDT v3. Ultra is a post-trained v3 with the same 25
  languages and similar speed, and lower word error rates in FluidAudio's
  published benchmarks.
- Ultra is opt-in. Choosing it asks first, then downloads about 630 MB from
  Hugging Face (v3 is about 480 MB) and verifies every file before use. If
  Ultra cannot be downloaded, verified, or loaded, Presspeech switches back to
  v3 and says so.
- The v3 copy stays on disk, so switching back needs no download. **Reset
  Speech Model Cache** resets only the selected model.
- Parakeet TDT v3 remains the default, and nothing changes unless you choose
  Ultra. The bundled FluidAudio speech runtime moves to 0.17.7; on the
  project's comparison recordings, v3 transcripts were unchanged.

#### Responsiveness

- Recording starts faster after the hotkey when the microphone was idle.
  Presspeech now prepares the audio input while idle without starting it, so
  the microphone and its recording indicator stay off until you press the
  hotkey. Built-in and USB microphones use this path; Bluetooth, aggregate,
  virtual, and other wireless inputs start as before.
- Each recording start writes one line of step timings to the local log,
  beginning `press timing:`. It contains durations only, with no key, app,
  window, or audio content.
- Presspeech no longer becomes unresponsive for minutes after a speech-model
  download finishes. Download progress rebuilt the menu for every received
  chunk; it now updates in the 5% steps the status already shows. This
  affected first-run model downloads as well as model switches.

#### Output mute

- On outputs with no mute control, such as many HDMI and DisplayPort displays,
  **Mute system audio while recording** now records without attempting to
  mute and notes this once in the local log, instead of logging a failed mute
  on every dictation. Outputs that can mute behave as before.

#### Diagnostics

- When automatic insertion stops and the transcript is copied for manual
  paste, the local log now says why: which destination check failed and at
  which step, a held modifier key, an unavailable paste key, or a Unicode
  typing limit. Delivery decisions are unchanged. App names, window titles,
  transcript text, and clipboard contents are not logged.

Audio and transcription remain local.

<a id="macos-0.3.9"></a>

### macOS 0.3.9 (2026-09-26)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.9)

The [full release notes](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.9) begin with a notice to read before opening this build.

#### Setup accessibility

- A clean install now waits for an explicit **Download Model** choice before
  starting the first ~500–600 MB speech-model download. Setup also shows the
  estimated free space needed for download and CoreML preparation before the
  choice. **Set Up Later** defers it; an approved download resumes on later
  launches. Existing installations keep their automatic startup, and a cached
  model loads without another prompt.
- Routine model-progress and permission-label updates in Setup Checklist now
  update the existing accessible elements instead of replacing the full view
  hierarchy. VoiceOver reading position, keyboard focus, and scroll position
  remain stable while those values change.
- Permission actions now distinguish **Continue** before the first microphone
  prompt from **Open Settings** for an earlier denial or system-settings grant;
  VoiceOver labels name the permission and action without implying Presspeech
  granted access itself.
- Once the model, audio input, and permissions are ready, **Try Dictation** is
  available even if the configured hotkey has not yet been tested. The
  scratchpad explains how to use the menu's **Start Dictation** and **Stop and
  Transcribe** actions instead; **Done** still requires a real hotkey event.

#### Language hints

- The macOS Language Hint menu now covers all 25 languages supported by the
  multilingual Parakeet model. Dutch, Danish, Swedish, Finnish, Hungarian,
  Estonian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Maltese, and Greek users can now select the
  same wrong-script filtering that was already available for the other model
  languages. Auto-detect remains the default.

#### Delivery authorization

- Setup now requires both focused-window Accessibility access and Quartz
  keyboard-event posting before declaring automatic delivery ready. A stale or
  separately denied posting grant can no longer make Presspeech report a paste
  that macOS silently discarded; diagnostics identify the two checks, and
  **Try Again** refreshes whichever represented TCC service is still missing.
- When exact-window capture is unavailable, the local log now distinguishes an
  Accessibility query failure from an invalid frontmost process or a focus
  change during the bounded query. These fixed categories include no app name,
  window title, field contents, or transcript text.
- If a required permission is missing when transcription completes or before
  delivery, Presspeech now finishes processing and keeps the complete
  transcript on the clipboard for manual paste. A grant that remains missing
  returns the app to permission setup; an observed interruption prevents that
  dictation from being pasted automatically even if the grant returns before
  delivery.
- Copy-only notices now say to use Command-V only if the clipboard has not
  changed. The menu notice can persist until the next dictation, so a later
  copy can replace the transcript; use Copy Last Transcript if it is available
  rather than pasting the newer item. This changes guidance, not clipboard
  ownership or automatic-paste behavior.
- Copying a History entry no longer clears an uncertain-delivery warning. A
  successful clipboard copy cannot establish whether the original field
  already contains all or part of the dictation; inspect it before pasting.

#### Model-download privacy

- Public speech-model downloads no longer inherit Hugging Face account tokens
  from `HF_TOKEN`, `HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN`, or
  `HUGGINGFACEHUB_API_TOKEN`. Presspeech removes those credentials only from
  its own process before FluidAudio can read them; the user's shell, token
  store, and other applications are unchanged.
- If that process-local removal unexpectedly fails, Presspeech refuses to
  start rather than allowing a public model request to carry an account
  credential. Diagnostics and logs contain variable names only, never token
  values.
- Malformed inherited `https_proxy` or `http_proxy` values now stop startup
  before FluidAudio can log the full proxy URL or silently ignore the intended
  route. The alert and app log identify only the setting name; correct or
  remove it before relaunching. Valid proxy settings still apply, and a
  trusted TLS-inspecting proxy can still read model-request headers.
- The previous macOS 0.3.8 release may have included an inherited Hugging Face
  token in a public model-download request, although the model needs no
  account token. This applies to model requests, not dictation audio or
  transcripts. The 0.3.9 change only removes credentials from Presspeech's
  process; it does not alter the user's shell or token store. If upgrading
  from 0.3.8, keep a working model cache and follow the
  [version-specific guidance](https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/privacy.html#macos-0-3-8-after-use)
  before a later model download.

#### Clipboard privacy

- **Keep Previous Clipboard for Manual Restore** now also retains an eligible
  previous clipboard when Presspeech uses clipboard-only recovery because the
  original focused window is unavailable or has changed. Interrupted direct
  Unicode fallback follows the same rule. The option remains off by default,
  and restoration still requires explicit confirmation.
- Automatic paste, focus-change recovery, **Copy Last Transcript**, and every
  copy or cut from **Try Dictation** now prepare transcript entries with
  AppKit's current-device-only option. They remain available to local
  Command-V but do not become available through Universal Clipboard.
- Transcript entries carry the standard transient, auto-generated, and
  concealed markers used by cooperating clipboard managers. The concealed
  marker additionally asks those tools not to display the transcript in clear
  text or persist it. macOS Clipboard History,
  third-party software that ignores those markers, and other local clipboard
  readers remain separate privacy boundaries.
- A saved previous clipboard is restored with its original items and formats,
  but is republished for the current Mac only. The original cross-device scope
  is not recoverable from the snapshot, so restoration fails private rather
  than making earlier content newly available through Universal Clipboard;
  Presspeech does not add transcript markers to the restored items.
- **Cut** in Try Dictation now keeps the selected text when its protected
  clipboard copy was replaced or the selection changed before deletion.
  Clipboard ownership can still change after the final check, so this is not
  an atomic cut guarantee.
- When macOS is configured to deny Presspeech pasteboard reads, dictation still
  replaces the clipboard with the transcript but skips the optional previous-
  clipboard snapshot without attempting to read it. The restore menu identifies
  the denied access instead of reporting a generic unavailable representation.

#### Diagnostic privacy

- Speech-recognition failures now write only a fixed failure event to the local
  log. Upstream decoder error descriptions are suppressed because they can
  include a partial recognition hypothesis.

Audio and transcription remain local. Clipboard text is not written to logs,
and these protections do not claim to prevent another local process from
reading the current pasteboard.

<a id="macos-0.3.8"></a>

### macOS 0.3.8 (2026-09-22)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.8)

The [full release notes](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.8) begin with a notice to read before opening this build.

This update fixes audio capture when input and output hardware use different
sample rates, strengthens automatic text delivery, and adds configurable
macOS hotkey combinations.

#### Audio reliability

- The capture tap now reads the selected microphone's hardware format instead
  of inheriting the output device's rate. This prevents apparently successful
  recordings from producing empty audio when, for example, a 48 kHz microphone
  is used alongside 44.1 kHz output.
- If macOS cannot convert a selected microphone's format to the 16 kHz mono
  stream required by speech recognition, audio startup now fails with a
  recovery message instead of appearing ready and silently discarding every
  recording.
- Recordings that end too quickly now say to speak longer instead of silently
  disappearing. A capture that returns no samples points to microphone recovery
  in the HUD, menu, Setup Checklist, VoiceOver, and diagnostics, with a direct
  **Check Microphone…** action in the menu and Dock menu.
- Setup Checklist identifies the selected microphone, explains when an
  unavailable saved device has fallen back to the system default, and provides
  a keyboard-accessible chooser beside the audio check.

#### Safer text delivery

- Presspeech preserves the frontmost process and exact Accessibility-focused
  window from recording through automatic paste. When the destination does
  not expose that window identity, delivery stays in manual clipboard recovery
  so an uncertain destination cannot receive an automatic paste.
- Automatic clipboard restoration and its delay presets are retired: a timer
  cannot establish that a slow destination has consumed the paste. The new
  **Keep Previous Clipboard for Manual Restore** option requires a fresh opt-in,
  including for users who previously enabled automatic restoration.
- With that option enabled, an eligible complete previous clipboard snapshot
  stays only in memory for up to five minutes. After checking that the latest
  dictated text arrived, choose **Restore Previous Clipboard…** and explicitly
  confirm.
  Cancel is the default; confirmation is not an operating-system acknowledgement.
- Consecutive dictations preserve the original snapshot and original deadline,
  which includes time asleep. Expiry, newer clipboard ownership, disabling the
  option or quitting discards the snapshot without an automatic rewrite.
  Clipboard ownership is checked after focus lookups and immediately before
  paste; a newer copy stops delivery. A stale confirmation cannot restore a
  different dictation's offer, and a failed restore never retries another write.
- Clipboard snapshots are capped at 64 MB and 256 representations. Oversized,
  unusually complex, incomplete, or concurrently changed clipboards are never
  retained as partial restore offers; dictation continues where ownership is
  stable, and the menu explains when the previous clipboard was not kept.
- Update checks accept only releases that GitHub marks immutable.

#### Flexible hotkeys

- Record Hotkey can now save combinations using Command, Control, or Option
  with another key, with optional Shift, alongside the existing right-side
  modifier and function-key choices.
- Complete combinations persist across restarts and work in hold or toggle
  mode. Unsafe shortcuts and ordinary unmodified typing keys remain blocked,
  and a binding that cannot be saved rolls back to the previous hotkey.
- Recording a modifier no longer triggers an AppKit exception. Releasing a
  right-side modifier preserves the selected combination when its left-side
  partner remains held, including keys held before the recorder opens.

#### Keyboard accessibility

- Interactive windows now request automatic Tab and Shift-Tab order
  recalculation. Setup Checklist also refreshes that order when it replaces
  controls, alongside its existing keyboard focus preservation.

#### Community compatibility evidence

- **Support → Test App Compatibility…** now opens the privacy-safe repeated
  target-app protocol directly from the app. The protocol collects aggregate
  delivery and focus-safety outcomes without asking users to publish dictated
  text.

#### Shareable diagnostics

- **Copy Diagnostics** now omits exact microphone names, raw startup errors,
  recent log lines and nonstandard application paths. It keeps status and
  configuration summaries useful for support; detailed errors remain in the
  local log for review before sharing.

Audio and transcription remain local. Transcript text and clipboard contents
are not written to the diagnostic log, and the global listener does not record
ordinary typed keys.

After installing this release, you can help verify automatic paste and safe
recovery in one target app by running the short, privacy-safe [compatibility
protocol](https://rcourtman.github.io/presspeech/app-compatibility.html).
Passing reports are useful too; share only aggregate outcomes from blank,
disposable fields, never dictated text or clipboard contents. Before sharing,
check the [support guide](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/blob/main/SUPPORT.md)
for a current reporting route. If issue creation is restricted and no
comparable open report accepts comments, keep the worksheet draft private and
retry later. A downloaded draft stays local; it is not submitted or monitored.
Do not send a report elsewhere as a workaround.

<a id="macos-0.3.7"></a>

### macOS 0.3.7 (2026-09-01)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.7)

This update keeps completed dictation bound to its original window and makes
setup, recovery, and core controls easier to reach without relying on a visible
menu-bar item or the default hotkey.

#### Safer text delivery

- Presspeech captures the destination before starting the audio engine and
  rechecks it before every automatic paste path.
- If focus changes while Presspeech is recording, transcribing, or preparing
  the clipboard, the transcript is copied for manual paste instead of being
  sent to the newly focused window.
- The menu-bar item keeps the **Copied — press ⌘V to paste** recovery action
  visible until the next dictation, even when transcript history is disabled.
  The recording indicator and VoiceOver announce the same recovery state.

#### Setup and recovery

- Setup Checklist now tracks the speech model, audio input, each permission,
  and the hotkey independently, with a retry or grant action beside the step
  that needs attention. It now waits for a real hotkey event before changing
  from **Close** to **Done**, rather than treating event-tap creation as proof
  that the configured key reaches Presspeech. The window is resizable and
  scrolls on smaller screens.
- Opening Presspeech again while it is already running brings Setup Checklist
  forward instead of silently doing nothing.
- **Show in Dock** provides a persistent alternative when the menu-bar item is
  hidden by a notch or a crowded menu bar. Its Dock menu exposes dictation,
  Settings, support, and recovery controls; the standard application menu also
  provides Settings and Command-comma while Dock mode is enabled.
- If macOS has registered Launch at Login but still needs approval, the setting
  says so and opens the relevant System Settings pane instead of turning the
  registration off.

#### Accessibility and controls

- Named **Start Dictation** and **Stop and Transcribe** menu actions provide a
  hotkey-free path and can be invoked with macOS Voice Control.
- The menu-bar control exposes loading, ready, recording, transcribing, and
  recovery states to VoiceOver.
- The recording indicator follows Reduce Motion, Reduce Transparency,
  Increase Contrast, and Differentiate Without Color as those settings change.
- Standard Edit and Window menus provide Undo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All,
  Close, Minimize, Zoom, and window discovery with the usual keyboard commands.
- Record Hotkey now previews a right-side modifier or F-key and waits for
  explicit confirmation instead of changing the shortcut on the first eligible
  keypress. Native Tab, Return, Space, and Escape dialog controls remain usable,
  and F-key choices explain when an Apple keyboard may require Fn.
- Dictation recovery instructions are announced to VoiceOver rather than being
  available only as a visual or audible cue.

#### Dictionary usability

- Large Dictionary & Shortcuts collections now open in a searchable manager
  with keyboard selection plus add, edit, and multi-item delete controls,
  instead of expanding into an impractically long menu.
- Double-clicking a rule opens it for editing, and a native shortcut menu puts
  Edit and multi-item Delete beside the selected rows for pointer and VoiceOver
  users. Truncated table cells expose their complete value in a tooltip.
- Invalid dictionary edits stay open with their draft text intact, focus the
  field that needs attention, and explain empty, oversized, unsupported, or
  full-library input instead of appearing to save an item that was discarded.

#### Stability

- The optional recording HUD now stays hidden instead of crashing if macOS
  temporarily reports no available displays during sleep or display
  reconfiguration.

Audio and transcription remain local. Transcript text, dictionary contents,
and shortcut contents are not written to the diagnostic log.

<a id="macos-0.3.6"></a>

### macOS 0.3.6 (2026-08-21)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.6)

This patch updates the local speech engine with upstream correctness fixes for
longer dictations and language hints.

#### Dictation reliability

- Long recordings preserve token order and content more reliably where the
  speech engine joins its 15-second processing windows.
- Final long-form windows align to the last speech-bearing audio instead of
  trailing silence, reducing the chance of lost content near release.
- Language hints no longer apply an English token blocklist outside the narrow
  French case it was designed for.
- Transient model-download failures preserve the existing cache instead of
  discarding usable files.

The notarised app zip is now roughly 8-9 MB rather than 2.5 MB because the
current FluidAudio package statically links additional support code. This does
not add another speech-model download, background service, or network call.
Audio and transcripts remain on the Mac, and transcript text never enters the
diagnostic log.

<a id="macos-0.3.5"></a>

### macOS 0.3.5 (2026-08-20)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.5)

This patch lets longer macOS dictations finish naturally while preserving the
automatic recording safety cutoff.

#### Configurable recording length

- Settings → Behavior → Maximum Recording Length now offers 1, 2, 5, and 10
  minute limits. The existing two-minute limit remains the default.
- Reaching the selected limit still stops, transcribes, and pastes the captured
  dictation, so a forgotten toggle cannot record indefinitely.
- Hand-written `max_recording_seconds` defaults values are constrained to 30
  seconds through 10 minutes to keep in-memory audio bounded.

There is no speech-model migration in this release. Audio and transcripts
remain on the Mac, and transcript text never enters the diagnostic log.

<a id="macos-0.3.4"></a>

### macOS 0.3.4 (2026-08-19)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.4)

This urgent patch fixes a macOS hotkey regression introduced in 0.3.3.

#### Hotkey reliability

- Dictation starts normally again when Presspeech is ready. Version 0.3.3
  incorrectly treated the ready state as if the app were terminating, so every
  hotkey press was rejected.
- The hotkey self-test now distinguishes a ready app, a temporarily blocked
  app, and an app that has actually terminated.

There is no speech-model migration in this release. Audio and transcripts
remain on the Mac, and transcript text never enters the diagnostic log.

<a id="macos-0.3.3"></a>

### macOS 0.3.3 (2026-08-15)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.3)

This patch makes the dictation hotkey recover cleanly when Presspeech is not
yet able to start another recording, and improves privacy-safe troubleshooting
for hotkey permission problems.

#### Hotkey reliability

- In toggle mode, a press received while the model is still loading or a
  transcription is in progress no longer consumes the next valid press. As
  soon as Presspeech is ready, the next press starts recording normally.
- Presspeech now records whether the macOS keyboard event tap is actually
  delivering events, helping distinguish a stale Input Monitoring grant from
  an unused hotkey.
- Diagnostics can identify an unmatched modifier key without recording
  ordinary keycodes or any typed text.

There is no speech-model migration in this release. Audio and transcripts
remain on the Mac, and transcript text never enters the diagnostic log.

<a id="macos-0.3.2"></a>

### macOS 0.3.2 (2026-07-23)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.2)

This patch makes the opt-in clipboard restoration path safer and more
reliable across applications with different paste timing.

#### Clipboard reliability

- Presspeech now waits longer after posting Command-V before restoring the
  previous clipboard, giving slower target applications time to consume the
  dictated text.
- Temporary transcript clipboard entries stay on the current Mac and carry
  standard transient markers, so cooperating clipboard managers do not retain
  text that exists only long enough to paste.
- Clipboard writes are assembled before Presspeech takes ownership, and stale
  snapshots are discarded if another application changes the clipboard. When
  safe restoration is not possible, Presspeech leaves the dictated text in
  place instead of risking clipboard data loss.

#### Speech model

The current FluidAudio candidates were re-evaluated on an expanded public
speech corpus. Parakeet TDT v3 remains the production model because it still
delivers the best accuracy and latency for Presspeech's push-to-talk workflow.
There is no speech-model migration in this release.

No audio, transcripts, settings, or clipboard contents leave the Mac.

<a id="macos-0.3.1"></a>

### macOS 0.3.1 (2026-07-22)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.1)

Presspeech now uses its own identity consistently across the app bundle,
preferences, correction documents, Application Support data, Homebrew
tap, and release tooling.

#### Clipboard restoration

- A new opt-in **Restore clipboard after paste** setting puts the previous
  clipboard contents back after a dictation paste. It is off by default.
- Restoration preserves multiple items and representations such as text,
  images, files, rich text, and links. If every representation cannot be
  copied safely, or the clipboard changes before restoration, Presspeech
  leaves the dictated text on the clipboard instead of risking data loss.

#### Upgrade notes

- Saved preferences, hotkey choices, local dictionary rules, correction
  sync configuration, and interrupted-audio recovery state migrate
  automatically on first launch.
- macOS privacy grants cannot be transferred between bundle identifiers.
  Setup Checklist opens automatically so you can grant Microphone,
  Accessibility, and Input Monitoring once to the current Presspeech
  identity.
- The Homebrew install and update command is now
  `brew update && brew upgrade --cask rcourtman/presspeech/presspeech`.

No audio, transcripts, settings, or migration data leave the Mac.

<a id="macos-0.3.0"></a>

### macOS 0.3.0 (2026-07-09)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.3.0)

Presspeech 0.3 establishes the current product identity and adds voice
shortcuts, spoken formatting, and a focused first-run dictation test.

#### New

- **Voice shortcuts** map a phrase you say to exact reusable text. They
  are deterministic, local, and managed alongside dictionary
  corrections.
- **Spoken formatting commands** optionally turn phrases such as “new
  line”, “new paragraph”, “bullet point”, “comma”, “open quote”, and
  parentheses into exact formatting without a rewriting model.
- **Try Dictation** opens a focused private scratchpad after setup, so
  the first hotkey test has an obvious destination.
- FluidAudio is updated to v0.15.5 after model-integrity, cold-download,
  latency, and real-dictation regression checks.

#### Upgrade notes

Homebrew users can run:

```sh
brew update
brew upgrade --cask rcourtman/presspeech/presspeech
```

After upgrading, launch `/Applications/Presspeech.app`. macOS shows its
standard downloaded-app confirmation on first launch; choose **Open**
after checking that Apple found no malicious software.

For a previous direct-download install, quit the installed copy, replace
it with `Presspeech.app`, and launch it once.

<a id="macos-0.2.20"></a>

### macOS 0.2.20 (2026-06-27)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.2.20)

#### What's Changed

- **Rapid dictation stability:** Presspeech now keeps the microphone engine warm
  briefly between rapid dictations instead of tearing CoreAudio down and
  rebuilding it after every release. This avoids a reproducible freeze after
  several quick uses while still closing the input session after the user
  pauses.
- **Audio route handling:** Configuration-change notifications caused by
  Presspeech's own audio-engine start/stop cycle are ignored, so they no longer
  trigger redundant deferred restarts during normal dictation.
- **Filler-word cleanup:** Removing a sentence-start filler inside a longer
  transcript now restores the capitalization of the next word. For example,
  `This is the first sentence. Um this is the second sentence.` now becomes
  `This is the first sentence. This is the second sentence.`

<a id="macos-0.2.16"></a>

### macOS 0.2.16 (2026-06-10)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.2.16)

#### What's Changed

- **Hotkey responsiveness:** System-audio mute calls, corrections-sync
  file checks, and update helpers now run off the main thread that
  services the global hotkey tap. A slow call (iCloud-synced corrections
  file, Homebrew, AppleScript) can no longer stall typing system-wide or
  cause macOS to drop a hotkey press.
- **Mute reliability:** If the system-audio mute succeeds but its
  verification read fails, Presspeech now keeps the crash-recovery marker
  and watchdog armed instead of tearing them down — the Mac can no
  longer be left muted with no recovery path. The mute lifecycle is now
  driven by pure, self-tested decision functions.
- **Toggle mode:** Pressing the hotkey while a transcription is still
  finishing no longer silently swallows presses; the toggle state only
  advances when a recording can actually start.
- **Filler-word removal:** Fixed punctuation artifacts with consecutive
  or sentence-final fillers ("So, um, uh, yes." no longer becomes
  "So,, yes."), and fillers before "?" or "!" are now cleaned up.
- **Update check:** "Remind me later" now survives relaunch instead of
  re-prompting shortly after the next launch. Manual check failures
  distinguish being offline from GitHub rate limiting and unexpected
  responses. The check now sends a fixed `presspeech-update-check`
  User-Agent, documented in the privacy table.
- **Text corrections:** Failed saves now surface an alert instead of
  silently dropping the edit, the corrections file cap is raised to
  4 MiB so maximum-size sets always fit, imports say when a file was
  truncated to the 512-entry cap, and sync no longer loses near-cap
  entries after a merge or skips an explicit "Sync Corrections Now"
  behind a stalled background scan.
- **Audio capture hardening:** Closed a data race on audio-converter
  state during engine stop/restart.
- **Text insertion:** The fallback typing path now posts matching
  key-up events so apps that track key state behave correctly.
- **Privacy documentation:** Now lists every model re-download trigger,
  the Homebrew hosts contacted during a user-triggered update, and the
  fact that the last transcript stays on the clipboard after pasting.
- **Release and CI hardening:** Release tags are annotated and pushed
  explicitly, releases run QA gates (CI-green check, self-test suite,
  packaged smoke test) before notarization, a `--cask-only` mode
  resumes half-finished releases, CI actions are SHA-pinned, the
  benchmark harness is compiled in CI, and docs deploy only after
  checks pass.

<a id="macos-0.2.15"></a>

### macOS 0.2.15 (2026-06-04)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.2.15)

#### What's Changed

- **Hotkey recovery:** Added **Settings -> Hotkey -> Reset Hotkey to
  Default** so a bad or awkward custom hotkey can be returned to Right Option
  without recording a replacement.
- **Hotkey recorder polish:** The recorder now accepts additional F-keys and
  right-side modifiers, rejects unsafe typing keys, and has stronger
  self-test coverage for save, rollback, and listener restart paths.
- **Speech model recovery guidance:** Startup failures now distinguish likely
  interrupted/corrupt model caches from network/download failures and point
  to **Support -> Reset Speech Model Cache...** when that is the right
  recovery path.
- **Unexpected-exit notice:** On the next launch after an abnormal exit,
  Presspeech offers to copy privacy-safe diagnostics or open the local log.
  Nothing is sent anywhere.
- **Mute recovery:** If Presspeech crashes or is force-quit while it muted
  system audio for an active recording, a local watchdog now unmutes the Mac
  when the app process disappears. The next launch also repairs any stale
  mute marker.
- **Audio capture hardening:** Recording samples are accumulated in segments
  and flattened outside the audio lock, with added downmix/converter
  self-tests.
- **Private benchmark tooling:** Added redacted real-dictation regression and
  power benchmark helpers. Their reports redact transcript text, fixture
  names, and local paths by default, and CI now runs their self-tests.
- **Release safety checks:** Added a packaged-app smoke script that verifies
  resources, signing, entitlements, and packaged self-tests.

<a id="macos-0.2.11"></a>

### macOS 0.2.11 (2026-05-21)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.2.11)

#### What's Changed

- **Hardened the update helper:** The script Presspeech writes to relaunch
  after a Homebrew upgrade now lives in the per-user temporary directory
  with mode `0600`, not in `/tmp` with a brief world-readable window.
  No user-facing behaviour change; closes a local file-permission gap.
- **Refuses sync through symlinks:** The text-corrections sync file is
  now checked with `lstat` before every periodic read and write. If the
  configured path is a symbolic link, Presspeech shows a "Sync Failed"
  alert and stops syncing instead of following the link. Protects
  against another local process planting a symlink at the persisted
  sync path.
- **Refuses to launch under a tampered model-download environment:** If
  `REGISTRY_URL` or `MODEL_REGISTRY_URL` is set in Presspeech's process
  environment, Presspeech now exits with a blocking alert pointing you at
  `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`, your shell rc files, and any parent
  process. FluidAudio uses those variables to redirect the speech-model
  download base URL, and Presspeech does not document either as a feature.
- **Setup Checklist polish:** Permission descriptions now name the
  exact System Settings breadcrumb and the control to flip. The
  TCC-reset tip explains the "Try Again" step explicitly, including the
  "doesn't appear in Settings" case. Checklist rows, separators, and
  the footer now share a single content width so the Status / Grant
  column no longer drifts between rows.
- **Documented the speech-model trust model:** `SECURITY.md` now spells
  out how the Parakeet TDT v3 weights reach the user (HTTPS from
  Hugging Face via FluidAudio, no cryptographic integrity check on the
  payload) and what the realistic abuse channel looks like.
- **Enabled Dependabot:** Weekly PRs for the single Swift dependency
  (FluidAudio) and the GitHub Actions used in `.github/workflows/`.
  Repo-side hygiene; no app-side change.

### macOS 0.2.4 (2026-05-13)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.2.4)

Reliability and control release. Improves hotkey handling, startup
readiness, microphone selection, cancellation, paste behavior, and
text-correction workflows. No migration steps — `brew upgrade --cask
presspeech` or the in-app **Update now…** button handles everything.

#### Dictation Reliability

- **Hotkey handling** — suppresses only the configured dictation hotkey,
  handles right-side modifier keys correctly, ignores F-key auto-repeat
  for recording transitions, and keeps the event-tap path responsive.
- **Startup readiness** — starts the audio engine before enabling
  dictation, blocks recording until required permissions are granted,
  and adds retry actions when speech model, audio input, or hotkey
  startup fails.
- **Audio recovery** — restores system audio if Presspeech quits during a
  muted recording and refreshes audio input after microphone route
  changes.

#### Settings And Workflow

- **Microphone selection** — adds a microphone picker, remembers the
  selected device, falls back cleanly when it is unavailable, and hides
  CoreAudio's default aggregate pseudo-device from the explicit list.
- **Recording control** — adds Escape/menu cancellation for active
  recordings without paste, history, or completion sound.
- **Paste behavior** — lets you append a space, append a newline, or add
  no suffix after pasted dictation.
- **Feedback sounds** — adds a setting to turn start/completion sounds
  off while keeping dictation behavior unchanged.

#### Text Corrections And Support

- **Recent transcript actions** — clears in-memory recent transcripts
  and can seed a new correction from the latest transcript without
  logging transcript text.
- **Diagnostics copy** — copies a transcript-free support summary with
  app, permission, microphone, and setting metadata.
- **Correction sharing cleanup** — removes temporary correction-share
  files after the share flow finishes or is dismissed.

#### Privacy

- No telemetry, analytics, crash reporting, cloud transcription, new
  Presspeech network call, or expanded entitlement was added.

### macOS 0.2.3 (2026-05-13)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.2.3)

Text correction portability release. Adds import, export, sharing,
and optional file-based sync for saved text corrections. No migration
steps — `brew upgrade --cask presspeech` or the in-app **Update now…**
button handles everything.

#### Text Corrections

- **Import and export** — save corrections as a `.presspeech-corrections`
  file, then bring them into another Mac with merge or replace.
- **Native sharing** — share the corrections file from the macOS share
  sheet, including AirDrop when available.
- **Optional sync file** — point Presspeech at a corrections file in
  iCloud Drive, Dropbox, Syncthing, or another synced folder. Presspeech
  reads and writes that local file; the folder provider handles
  moving it between Macs.
- **Double-click import** — `.presspeech-corrections` files are registered
  as Presspeech documents and can be opened with the app.

#### Privacy

- Sync does not add a Presspeech account, backend, or new direct network
  call. Correction files are readable JSON so they remain portable and
  auditable.

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.2.2)

Text correction release. Adds a local corrections dictionary for

#### Text Corrections

- **Local correction dictionary** — add replacement pairs from

- **Whole-word and phrase matching** — corrections apply after
  transcription and before paste/history, with longest matches
  winning when entries overlap.

  preferences. Audio still stays on-device, transcripts are still
  never written to disk, and logs only record how many corrections
  were applied.

  render reliably inside the menu-triggered dialog.

  `clawed` → `Claude` example.

<a id="macos-0.2.0"></a>

### macOS 0.2.0 (2026-05-11)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/v0.2.0)

**Presspeech is now a native Swift app.** Same UX — push-to-talk, menu
bar, no preferences window — rebuilt on the Apple Neural Engine via
[FluidAudio](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio) +
[Parakeet TDT v3](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3).

- **~100 ms** from key release to pasted text (down from ~180 ms)
- **2.2 MB** download (down from ~150 MB)
- Two hardened-runtime entitlements instead of six
- No embedded interpreter, no JIT, no library-validation override

#### Upgrading from v0.1.x

`brew upgrade --cask presspeech` or the in-app **Update now…** button
handles the swap. Settings, granted permissions, and Skip-version
state carry over cleanly — same bundle id, same Developer ID cert.

**Heads up: v0.2.0 requires macOS 26 (Tahoe).** If you're on macOS
13, 14, or 15, the upgrade will refuse with a brew error — stay on
v0.1.6 until you can upgrade macOS.

##### Reclaiming disk space (optional)

The old MLX model cache from v0.1.x is no longer used. ~600 MB:

```sh
rm -rf ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--mlx-community--parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2
```

If you ever installed v0.1.x from a source clone via `install.sh`,
the LaunchAgent it created is also unused now:

```sh
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.local.presspeech.plist 2>/dev/null
rm -f ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.local.presspeech.plist
```

## Windows

<a id="windows-0.1.12"></a>

### Windows 0.1.12 (2026-09-22)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/windows-v0.1.12)

The [full release notes](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/windows-v0.1.12) begin with a notice to read before opening this build.

Presspeech for Windows 0.1.12 recovers from microphone hardware changes
without requiring an app restart and refreshes the pinned CUDA runtime.

#### Audio-device recovery

- If a selected or automatic microphone disappears, Presspeech can safely
  refresh PortAudio's device table and retry discovery when the device is
  reconnected. A specifically selected device still fails safely rather than
  silently switching to a different microphone.
- Process-wide coordination prevents a device refresh from terminating
  PortAudio while a recording, microphone check, stream construction, or
  device query is active. Slow driver work does not hold the app state lock,
  and stale discovery from an earlier recording cannot overwrite a newer one.
- Native streams whose first close attempt fails remain protected and are
  retried before any later backend reset, avoiding unsafe recovery around a
  handle that the audio driver may still consider live.

#### Release runtime

- The Windows CUDA package now pins Torch 2.14.0 with CUDA 12.6, and the
  resolved Python 3.12.10 release graph remains locked and reproducible.

#### Installation and updates

- Uninstall now removes the current user's Presspeech startup entry, preventing
  Windows from trying to launch a removed executable at sign-in.
- Update checks accept only releases that GitHub marks immutable. Publication
  verifies the release attestation and both installer and checksum assets.
- Before publication, the hosted Windows runner checks the finished installer's
  install, packaged self-test, startup-entry cleanup, and uninstall behavior.

This remains a prerelease. The complete microphone, target-app, upgrade, and
assistive-technology qualification matrix is still required before stable promotion.

Speech recognition remains entirely local, and transcript and dictionary text
remain excluded from diagnostics. This build is not yet code-signed, so
Windows SmartScreen may show **Unknown publisher**; choose **More info → Run
anyway** only where local policy permits, after verifying the supplied SHA-256
checksum.

<a id="windows-0.1.11"></a>

### Windows 0.1.11 (2026-09-01)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/windows-v0.1.11)

Presspeech for Windows 0.1.11 keeps completed dictation bound to its original
window and makes setup, recovery, and core controls easier to use without
depending on the notification-area icon or the default hotkey.

#### Safer text delivery

- Presspeech captures the destination process and window before recording and
  rechecks them before every automatic paste path, including Try Dictation.
- If the destination is unavailable or focus changes during recording or
  transcription, the transcript remains on the clipboard for manual paste
  instead of being sent to the newly focused window.

#### Setup and recovery

- Setup checks microphone input and waits for the selected speech model to be
  ready before it can finish. Failed checks expose retry and recovery actions.
- Computers without usable CUDA now start with the CPU-capable Whisper
  `base.en` model instead of selecting a GPU-only model that cannot load.
- Changing models starts preparation immediately and reports loading, ready,
  and failed states without consuming the next dictation attempt.
- Launching Presspeech again restores its existing window, or opens Setup or
  Settings, rather than silently doing nothing.
- Setup and Settings report global-hotkey readiness and can replace a failed
  or stopped keyboard listener without requiring access to the tray icon.
- Press **Escape** or choose **Cancel Dictation (Esc)** to discard an active
  recording without transcription or clipboard changes.

#### Accessibility and controls

- Setup, Settings, update, and Try Dictation windows expose names, roles,
  values, and actions through Windows UI Automation, with access keys and
  screen-reader announcements for important status changes.
- Dialogs are resizable and scroll on smaller or scaled displays. The recording
  indicator follows Windows DPI and high-contrast colours.
- Setup can apply a different hotkey before completion, so a conflicting
  default key no longer blocks first run.
- When Windows blocks simulated input into an app running as administrator,
  Presspeech leaves the transcript on the clipboard and explains how to paste
  it safely instead of silently losing the delivery attempt.

#### Recognition and language

- Whisper models use reviewed immutable snapshots, do not carry text from the
  previous recording into the next one, and filter silence before decoding.
- British spelling conversion now covers common inflections consistently.

Release dependencies are pinned to an exact Windows and Python 3.12.10 graph.
Speech recognition remains entirely local, and transcript and dictionary text
remain excluded from diagnostics. This build is not yet code-signed, so
Windows SmartScreen may show **Unknown publisher**; choose **More info → Run
anyway** after verifying the supplied SHA-256 checksum.

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/windows-v0.1.8)

Presspeech for Windows 0.1.8 closes the remaining replacement window when an

<a id="windows-0.1.2"></a>

### Windows 0.1.2 (2026-08-05)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/windows-v0.1.2)

Presspeech for Windows 0.1.2 fixes playback muting on PCs with more than one
active audio output.

#### Fixed

- Dictation now mutes every active Windows playback endpoint, rather than only
  the default multimedia device. This covers audio routed separately to a
  headset, Realtek speakers, HDMI output, or another active endpoint.
- Every endpoint's original mute state is saved and restored independently.
- A failure on one endpoint no longer prevents other endpoints from being
  muted or safely restored, and the log records endpoint counts and failures.

Speech recognition remains entirely local. This build is not yet code-signed,
so Windows SmartScreen may show **Unknown publisher**; choose **More info →
Run anyway** after verifying the supplied SHA-256 checksum.

<a id="windows-0.1.1"></a>

### Windows 0.1.1 (2026-08-05)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/windows-v0.1.1)

Presspeech for Windows 0.1.1 makes first launch and ongoing maintenance clearer
without changing the fast, local dictation path.

#### What's new

- First-run readiness window showing model status, microphone selection,
  push-to-talk key, and Start with Windows
- Optional privacy-safe daily update checks plus a manual tray-menu check
- User-approved installer downloads verified against the GitHub asset size and
  published SHA-256 before Presspeech offers to run them
- Copy Diagnostics tray action with runtime and configuration metadata but no
  transcript, audio, or dictionary contents
- Atomic settings writes for safer background update checks and UI saves

#### Privacy and signing

Speech recognition remains entirely local. Update checks send a fixed User-Agent
and ordinary HTTPS metadata only; no app version, device identifier, settings,
audio, transcript, or usage counts are attached.

This build is not yet code-signed. Windows SmartScreen may show **Unknown
publisher**; choose **More info → Run anyway** after verifying the SHA-256
checksum supplied with the installer.

<a id="windows-0.1.0"></a>

### Windows 0.1.0 (2026-08-05)

[GitHub release](https://github.com/rcourtman/presspeech/releases/tag/windows-v0.1.0)

First packaged Windows release of Presspeech.

#### What is included

- Self-contained Windows x64 installer: no Python or command-line setup required
- NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 with CUDA acceleration and duration-aware decoding
- Whisper fallbacks, British spelling, local dictionary rules, audio cues, playback muting, and visual status indicator
- Right Alt hold-to-talk, configurable hotkeys, deterministic microphone selection, and Start with Windows support
- Local-only audio processing with no accounts, telemetry, or transcript logging

#### Requirements and first launch

- Windows 10 or 11, x64
- A current NVIDIA driver is strongly recommended for the default Parakeet model
- About 4.4 GB for the installed app, plus about 2.5 GB for the first-run model download

This build is not yet code-signed. Windows SmartScreen may show **Unknown publisher**; choose **More info → Run anyway** after verifying the SHA-256 checksum supplied with the installer.
